faqs.q: What makes Fracture different from other Valorant maps?
faqs.a: Fracture has an H-shaped layout in which attackers can approach each site from two directions, using ziplines to cross the middle of the map. This makes flanks and surprise rotations far more common than on most maps, so communication and watching your back matter a lot.

faqs.q: Why is Fracture considered hard to defend?
faqs.a: Because attackers can hit each site from two sides, defenders often have to split their attention and can easily be caught in a pinch. Sentinels with traps or alarms, and initiators who gather information early, help defenders spot where the attack is coming from and rotate in time.

faqs.q: Do you need two initiators on Fracture?
faqs.a: Not always, but information is very valuable on Fracture, so many teams run two initiators to scout both approaches and support plants and retakes. One initiator plus a sentinel who watches flanks can also work, as long as someone on the team is reliably gathering intel.

faqs.q: Why can't I find Fracture in competitive matches?
faqs.a: Riot rotates maps in and out of the competitive pool from time to time, so Fracture may be missing in some acts. Check the current map pool in the game or in the latest patch notes; when a map is out of rotation, you can usually still practise on it in custom games.
